turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I'm here about the zero on Owen's Hamlet essay. Who decided it?

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Mr. Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still want the zero on Owen's Hamlet essay withdrawn, an apology for entering it before anyone called me, and a clear answer on who decided it. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position, wanting the zero withdrawn, an apology, and a meeting with the principal, with nothing agreed; the fair outcome, a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, was never reached because the meeting ended before you spoke.
What moved her: Nothing, because no evidence, ownership or offer was put in front of her.
What cost ground: Nothing, because you ended the meeting before saying anything that could help or hurt your case.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your evidence never came near that night because none was shown; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asks who decided the zero, start by owning that it went into the gradebook before her family was called, then show her one dated document tied to Owen's own work.
